title: Triage Ribbon: SLO-aware Alert Composer + Incident Handoff Panel
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Engineers need a faster, context-rich way to triage alerts from the Console that ties directly to SLO health and reduces noisy handoffs between on-call engineers. Current alert composer and incident pages are separated from SLO context and require manual steps to attach postmortems and create on-call handoff notes. Goal: Design a compact "triage ribbon" that surfaces SLO context, suggested severity and runbook links in the alert composer, plus a lightweight incident handoff panel that creates deep links to postmortem drafts and on-call notes.
acceptance_criteria: When creating or editing an alert, the composer shows the linked SLO name, current error budget burn (percent), and suggested severity based on configured thresholds.
The triage ribbon appears in the top of an alert details modal and contains three primary actions: Acknowledge, Assign, Create Handoff Note.

Create Handoff Note opens a small panel pre-populated with incident summary, SLO context, and a deep-link to a postmortem template in Drive. Saving the handoff produces a persistent quick-link in the incident header.
All elements meet AA color contrast and keyboard navigation standards; ribbon actions are operable without a mouse.
Design tokens and component specs provided so the engineering team can implement with the Console design system. Figma file includes interactive prototype for desktop and tablet breakpoints.
The feature includes telemetry hooks defined in the design doc for adoption tracking (composer open, acknowledge, handoff created).

notes: Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Visibility vs noise: decided on top-of-modal ribbon with subtle border and collapse state to reduce clutter. 2) Privacy: postmortem deep links default to draft-sharing permission; handoff UI surfaces permission tips before saving. 3) SLO data freshness: use a cached SLO snapshot with an explicit 'refresh' affordance to avoid blocking UI on slow SLO queries. 4) Accessibility: ribbon actions exposed to screen readers with ARIA live region updates for state changes.
implementation_notes: Engineering needs: (a) endpoint /api/internal/slo-snapshot?alert_id= that returns SLO percent and burn rate; (b) telemetry events: console.triage.open, console.triage.ack, console.triage.assign, console.triage.handoff.create; (c) small DB table for persistent handoff quick-links (minimal schema). Backend work tracked in ENG-2198 and ENG-2045. Frontend PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2790.
next_steps: Engineering spike for SLO snapshot endpoint (ENG-2198)
Prototype usability session with 6 on-call engineers (schedule in 2025-W09)
Create QA checklist for keyboard and screen reader flows
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Composer open latency could degrade if SLO queries are slow. Mitigation: use cached snapshot and async refresh.
Risk: On-call handoff could leak sensitive links. Mitigation: surface permission guidance and default to draft-sharing.
Risk: Increased cognitive load for junior engineers. Mitigation: include simple 'suggested action' microcopy and link to onboarding doc.
review_feedback: Anya Gupta (Eng): Backend contract looks reasonable; add bulk rate-limit for SLO snapshot endpoint.
Sasha Kim (Security): Good to include permission copy; suggest logging when external links are created.
Tom Reynolds (Design Lead): Visual is good; prefer 40px ribbon height for clarity on dense pages.
Sara Velasquez (PM): Add metric: reduction in time-to-ack for alerts tied to SLOs as success criteria.
estimate_notes: 5 points covers final mockups, microcopy, accessibility refinements, and handoff docs. Engineering implementation split into two sprints (ENG-2198 backend spike + ENG-2045 frontend).
